cards.explanation: The answer is John the Baptist. He's on the list the disciples give Jesus. He's the one who came baptizing and preaching in the wilderness (Mark 1:4). Elijah and one of the prophets are the other guesses people had. So some people were naming John when they talked about who Jesus was.
The answer is Peter. Jesus asks, “Who do you say I am?” and Peter is the one who answers. Peter is one of the twelve (Mark 3:16). Out of all of them, Peter is the one the text shows answering.
The answer is Christ. Peter answers Jesus, “You are the Christ.” The disciples had just told Jesus what other people were saying, and Peter gave Him this answer instead. That's a big answer, friends.

The answer is False. After Peter's answer, the text says Jesus “…warned them not to tell anyone about Him.” That's the opposite of telling everyone. The text doesn't give a reason, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is that He must suffer and be killed. Jesus says the Son of Man “…must suffer many things…” and “…must be killed…” He says it plain and doesn't dress it up. That's a hard thing to hear, and I think it was hard for the disciples too.

The answer is True. Jesus says the Son of Man must be killed “…and after three days rise again.” The hard news doesn't have the last word, and Jesus says so in the same breath. Don't skip the end of that sentence, friends.

The answer is False. Peter began to rebuke Jesus, and Jesus answers by rebuking Peter. He says, “Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.” Jesus doesn't go along with what Peter says.

The answer is the things of men. Jesus says Peter does not have in mind “…the things of God, but the things of men.” It's a strong word from Jesus, so I think it stings. One sentence, two sides, friends.

The answer is follow. Jesus says, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.” Coming after Him means following Him. Simple words, and a big thing to say yes to.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.” It's backwards from how we'd think, and He says it anyway. Read it twice if you need to, friends, I did.

The point is that nothing is worth trading your soul for. Jesus asks, “What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?” Two questions, and the whole world isn't a good trade. I think He wants us to sit with that.

The answer is ashamed. Jesus says, “If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation…” Then He says the Son of Man will also be ashamed of that person when He comes in His Father's glory with the holy angels. It's a serious line, so I'll keep my jokes in the oven.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels.” It's a sober moment, and the verse says it plainly. I'll let Jesus' words stand just as He said them.

The answer is the kingdom of God arriving with power. Jesus says, “…there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God arrive with power.” He opens with “Truly I tell you…” so He's saying it plainly. The time He gives is before some of those standing there taste death, friends.
